newsitem.title: USA: IMF aims to help clamp down on money launderers.
newsitem.headline: IMF aims to help clamp down on money launderers.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund will help member countries to clamp down on money laundering, IMF managing director Michel Camdessus said Thursday.

Camdessus told a news conference that the IMF and the World Bank, together with the regional development banks, stood ready to provide countries with funding and technical advice to combat that crime.
"We are going to make life a little more difficult for launderers," he said at the end of the IMF/World Bank annual meeting.
Camdessus endorsed studies conducted by IMF economists who concluded that money laundering could jeopardize countries' financial systems and harm their macroeconomic stability.

In the course of reviewing the health of countries' banking sectors, the IMF will advise governments on the strength of their regulations and enforcement procedures in order to close the gaps that allow criminals to launder money.
Regarding banking secrecy laws -- on which many off-shore banking industries are founded -- Camdessus said the IMF had not yet discussed them with member countries who have such rules on their books.
Once it has studied the impact of such laws on money laundering, the IMF could make a recommendation to countries on whether they should scrap those rules.
